summary.text: Network and infrastructure engineer with hands-on L2/L3 operations across a 1,000+ system, 70-subnet enterprise estate: L3-to-L2 migrations, VLAN trunking, Active Directory DNS, and firewall drop-log RCA in Splunk. Automates network operations in Python (Netmiko, NetworkX, SQLite): built and led a 4-site physical switch survey covering 2,000+ network devices, parsed multi-vendor CLI output (Cisco, HP, D-Link, Huawei, Aruba) into a validated schema, and cut the manual baseline from 4 months to under 2. Held 24/7 solo L1/L2 operations for 3 consecutive months with 100% first-contact resolution and zero escalations. Serving notice period, last working day 25 September 2026.

experience.context: Enterprise IT outsourcing for Honeywell (Endpoint Operations + network estate): large-scale system configuration, bare-metal imaging, network access control, deployment operations and platform reliability across a 1,000+ system, 70-subnet estate. Also led the Bangalore-client physical network survey: built the automation toolkit, then ran the survey across 4 sites and 2,000+ network devices, delivering in under 2 months against a 4-month manual baseline.

achievements.what: Automated configuration management and OS vulnerability patching across 1,000+ distributed systems via Tanium + PowerShell.
achievements.why: Manual patching could not keep up with compliance requirements.
achievements.impact: 98% compliance on targeted vulnerabilities; eliminated manual configuration drift.
achievements.evidence: Tanium Deploy + PowerShell, client compliance reporting

achievements.what: Developed a Python automation suite (Netmiko) for switch surveys, then extended it into a full field-to-report toolkit (Tkinter capture GUI, SQLite warehouse, NetworkX topology inference, Graphviz diagrams) and led the survey with it across 4 sites and 2,000+ network devices.
achievements.why: Manual per-device surveys took too long, wasted address space, and could not be audited or re-run.
achievements.impact: Survey delivered in under 2 months against a 4-month manual baseline; reclaimed 500+ unused IPs; ~90 topology diagrams plus inventory, vendor and port-capacity reports.
achievements.evidence: network-survey-automation (public, sanitised): 4 sites, ~700 managed switches, 100,000+ MAC-table entries

achievements.what: Automated ServiceNow privileged account provisioning using custom PowerShell (WMI/RDP) tooling.
achievements.why: Manual provisioning took ~5 minutes per account.
achievements.impact: 95% faster provisioning (5 minutes to under 20 seconds).

achievements.what: Engineered zero-prompt PowerShell automation scripts for configuration deployments, replacing a legacy 3,000-line manual workflow and accelerating the automated provisioning pipeline.
achievements.why: Legacy manual workflow was slow, error-prone and required operator prompts at every step.
achievements.impact: Replaced 3,000-line manual workflow; faster, unattended provisioning pipeline.
achievements.evidence: Production use in enterprise deployment operations

achievements.what: Delivered L1/L2 enterprise endpoint support: bare-metal OS imaging, hardware provisioning and complex system configuration for high-priority deployments (Windows Autopilot / Intune enrollment).
achievements.why: High-priority end-user deployments need reliable, repeatable provisioning.
achievements.impact: Accelerated the Windows Autopilot / Intune enrollment pipeline.

achievements.what: Managed DNS Forwarders within Active Directory and facilitated L3-to-L2 network migrations across 70 subnets (defining firewall ports/URLs, managing AD DNS), with RCA on blocked ports and URLs from Splunk firewall drop logs to restore lab application connectivity.
achievements.why: Network reorganization to simplify routing and reduce complexity; blocked traffic needed a root cause, not a workaround.
achievements.impact: Clean migration across 70 subnets with no service disruption; blocked lab application traffic root-caused and restored.

achievements.what: Reconstructed L2 topology where discovery data was incomplete: classified switch roles (Core/Distribution/Access) from graph degree and betweenness centrality, inferred switch-to-switch uplinks from shared MAC tables, de-duplicated LLDP/CDP neighbours across identifier forms, and propagated network segment IDs top-down from the Floor Access Switch.
achievements.why: Not every link was visible: unmanaged hops hid segments and many external devices reported no hostname, so the topology had to be inferred rather than read from a complete discovery set.
achievements.impact: Usable L1/L2 topology maps and uplink reports from partial CDP/LLDP and MAC-table data, with an isolated-from-FAS flag per switch.

achievements.what: Ran 24/7 solo overnight L1/L2 operations for 3 consecutive months, owning the full incident queue: first-line network and endpoint troubleshooting plus bare-metal OS imaging and hardware provisioning for high-priority deployments.
achievements.why: The estate needed unattended overnight coverage with no L2 backstop on shift.
achievements.impact: 100% first-contact resolution, zero escalations and zero tickets raised to L3.

achievements.what: Managed enterprise infrastructure operations: automated system configurations, network access control, and platform reliability engineering for high-priority deployments.
achievements.why: Enterprise needs consistent, reliable, repeatable platform state.
achievements.impact: Reliable high-priority deployment operations.

projects.name: Network Survey Automation - Field-to-Report Toolkit
projects.context: Public, sanitised rebuild of the in-house network survey toolkit used on the Bangalore client estate (synthetic data only): Tkinter field-capture GUI, staged LLM + Pydantic extraction, SQLite warehouse, NetworkX topology inference and Graphviz diagram generation. ~20k LOC Python, source-available non-commercial license.

achievements.what: Built a Tkinter field-capture GUI on a deterministic building-floor-wing-area folder convention, so hundreds of console logs captured independently by different surveyors resolve from metadata alone with no manual index.
achievements.why: Survey metadata was being recorded in different shapes by different people, which made downstream matching slow and inconsistent.
achievements.impact: Consistent machine-readable metadata and no manual log-to-device mapping across 4 sites.

achievements.what: Parsed raw multi-vendor CLI logs (Cisco, HP, D-Link, Huawei, Aruba) into a strict JSON schema with a staged LLM + Pydantic v2 pipeline: Stage 1A (device fields), Stage 1B (segment association), Stage 2 (MAC table chunked to 100 rows), run over a rate-limit-aware process pool with per-device retry.
achievements.why: Per-vendor TextFSM/regex templates could not cover a multi-vendor estate captured with different commands, and a single mega-prompt over a full CLI dump was unreliable.
achievements.impact: Every extracted record validated before it reaches the database; malformed model output fails loudly instead of poisoning the warehouse.

achievements.what: Stored survey data in a normalised 16-table SQLite warehouse (interfaces, VLANs, IP interfaces, MAC and ARP tables, LLDP/CDP neighbours, routing table, segment maps) and drove Excel/CSV reporting off it: device inventory, vendor summary, port capacity, standard/non-standard classification and unassigned-network extraction.
achievements.why: Spreadsheets could not express the joins the analysis needed across devices, interfaces, MAC tables and neighbours.
achievements.impact: Auditable survey results and 500+ unused IPs identified for reclaim across 4 sites.

achievements.what: Generated ~90 Pydot/Graphviz topology diagrams clustered by inferred switch role, each with a machine-readable uplink JSON sidecar, and routed model uncertainty into a human review queue that keeps validated and reviewed artefacts separate.
achievements.why: Non-engineers needed readable maps, and review corrections had to survive a re-run of the LLM stage.
achievements.impact: Repeatable diagrams plus uplink reports at production scale (4 sites, ~700 managed switches, 100,000+ MAC-table entries).

projects.name: Zero-Trust Cloud Infrastructure & GitOps Pipeline
projects.context: Public case-study repo (roguehunter7/Portfolio) demonstrating zero-ingress infrastructure on free-tier cloud (GCP + Oracle Cloud), deployed keyless from GitHub Actions; site served at the edge on Cloudflare Pages behind a Cloudflare Tunnel.

achievements.what: Declaratively provisioned a zero-trust GCP environment with Terraform: custom VPC, deny-all ingress firewall (0-65535), IAP-only SSH (35.235.240.0/20), e2-micro instance, state-locked GCS backend.
achievements.why: Reproducible infra, no click-ops, and no public ingress by construction.
achievements.impact: One codebase yields VPC + firewalls + VM; zero exposed management ports.

achievements.what: Provisioned an Oracle Cloud Always Free A1.Flex (2 OCPU/12 GB) Hermes host from the same IaC with no security group: sshd binds loopback and admin arrives as SSH carried by the Cloudflare Tunnel, gated by Access; CI never needs a shell on the box.
achievements.why: Extend the zero-ingress pattern to a second cloud without paying.
achievements.impact: $0/mo cross-cloud compute; shell access only through the Cloudflare tunnel.

achievements.what: Enforced tenancy-wide cost guardrails in IaC: a budget alerting on any spend ($1 / $0.01 threshold) plus quota that zeros all compute/memory families then re-allows exactly the Always-Free A1 allowance.
achievements.why: Guarantee the account stays at $0 even on PAYG.
achievements.impact: No resource outside the free tier can launch; automatic spend alerts.

achievements.what: Built a keyless CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions using Workload Identity Federation (WIF) and OIDC: IAP-SSH deploys for the vault host and wrangler pages deploy for the site under a hardened _headers policy (HSTS, nosniff, frame denial, Permissions-Policy; no CSP by design); the Hermes host restores its own state from Object Storage at first boot, so CI never needs a shell on it.
achievements.why: No long-lived cloud credentials in CI; static content served at the edge.
achievements.impact: Zero static keys; one commit renders the ATS-safe resume PDF and publishes the site.

achievements.what: Built a lighter serverless phase: a low-latency visitor tracker + session analytics API in Go (Golang) on Google Cloud Run, with transactional state and atomic increments in Cloud Firestore (Native Mode), automated expired-session cleanup (no DB bloat), and strict HTTP Cache-Control headers.
achievements.why: Prove the stack could run serverless on free-tier without VM maintenance.
achievements.impact: Real-time session/page-view metrics with transactional, bloat-free state.
achievements.evidence: Go API + Cloud Run + Firestore (later reverted to the $0 Docker/VM phase)

achievements.what: Isolated services on a private Docker Compose network reached only through an outbound Cloudflare Tunnel (remote-managed), exposing zero host ports.
achievements.why: Inbound-only via an outbound connection; nothing reachable from the internet except through Cloudflare.
achievements.impact: Zero host ports exposed; $0/month across the stack.

projects.name: Hermes: Self-Hosted AI Assistant
projects.context: Always-on personal AI assistant (Telegram gateway + DeepSeek API) running natively under systemd on the zero-ingress Oracle A1.Flex box. It brings its own uv-managed Python and Node, sshd loopback-only and the dashboard auth-gated behind ufw; provisioned end-to-end by Terraform + cloud-init.

achievements.what: Installed the assistant natively as a dedicated `hermes` systemd user: the official installer brings uv-managed Python, Node and ripgrep into its own home, so the distro's versions are never in the dependency path and a monthly apt upgrade cannot break the agent.
achievements.why: Own the stack directly on the box with one service to supervise, with no container layer in the way.
achievements.impact: The agent and its runtime move forward together; `hermes update` rolls the checkout back if the pulled code does not parse.

achievements.what: Snapshotted the agent's state to a private OCI Object Storage bucket every six hours using the instance principal (no API key on the box), and made the host restore the newest snapshot itself at first boot. A rebuild is one workflow run, and a reset wipes the instance and the bucket for a factory-fresh agent.
achievements.why: The box is disposable; the agent's sessions, skills and memories are not.
achievements.impact: A rebuild is one workflow run with at most six hours of state loss; restore refuses archives with absolute or parent-traversal paths.

achievements.what: Wired the assistant to the DeepSeek API (v4-flash everywhere) for main and all auxiliary tasks.
achievements.why: DeepSeek's budget tier is ~10x cheaper than Gemini paid (which needed a ₹1000 minimum top-up).
achievements.impact: Near-zero cost; single rate-limit and billing bucket.

achievements.what: Kept a strict zero-ingress posture: no security group, ufw denies inbound, sshd loopback-only, and the dashboard reachable only through the Cloudflare Tunnel behind Access, with its own username/password gate enforced.
achievements.why: Nothing inbound is reachable from the internet, yet admin and the dashboard still work from anywhere.
achievements.impact: No reachable listener; the host is invisible to port scanners and the dashboard still requires a login.
achievements.evidence: ufw deny-inbound + sshd loopback :22, dashboard :9119 auth-gated

projects.name: Vaultwarden: Zero-Ingress Self-Hosted Password Vault
projects.context: The freed GCP e2-micro re-purposed into a hardened self-hosted password manager: loopback-only on :8000 behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, a least-privilege service account, and nightly SQLite backups to a private GCS bucket.

achievements.what: Ran Vaultwarden as a single container bound to loopback :8000 with a cloudflared container behind a remote-managed Cloudflare Tunnel (vault.sreeramkr.com).
achievements.why: A credential store must have no reachable management surface.
achievements.impact: Deny-all firewall + IAP-only SSH; zero public ports.

achievements.what: Handled secrets with strict hygiene: Argon2 admin token and config in a root-owned 0600 .env written by CI (correct $ escaping), signups disabled, short admin session lifetime.
achievements.why: Signups off and secrets never baked into images or the repo.
achievements.impact: Admin reachable only through the tunnel; no leaked credentials.

achievements.what: Backed up nightly using a least-privilege SA (roles/storage.objectUser) on one private GCS bucket, uploading the SQLite DB via the instance's metadata token and pruning to the newest 10.
achievements.why: No keys on the host; the backup SA can never touch the tfstate bucket.
achievements.impact: Credential-free, auto-pruned off-site backups at $0.

projects.name: CornerSentinel: IoT Safety System (Li-Fi Communication)
projects.context: Capstone project: a real-time computer-vision warning system on Raspberry Pi to prevent accidents at blind corners, using Li-Fi (Visible Light Communication) for low-latency signaling.

achievements.what: Developed a real-time computer vision warning system (Python, YOLOv8, OpenCV) on Raspberry Pi to detect pedestrians/vehicles at blind corners and trigger a warning.
achievements.why: Prevent accidents at blind corners where line-of-sight is obstructed.
achievements.impact: Working edge CV prototype on commodity hardware.

achievements.what: Implemented Li-Fi (Visible Light Communication) signaling to transmit the warning, achieving low-latency optical data transmission and signal modulation.
achievements.why: Traditional radio/wireless signaling had latency and cost drawbacks for a short-range autonomous warning.
achievements.impact: 1ms warning signal latency via Li-Fi.
